headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error paths exist because Airbyte can egress broadly while Khoj reads indexed personal documents and sends context to cloud or configured search providers.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can emit data through its API and broad network egress, while Khoj reads indexed files and supports RAG/web search. If Airbyte-fed content is later indexed into Khoj, malicious text could be treated as instructions. No shared channel is explicit, so this is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into Khoj-indexed notes or documents
IF Khoj treats retrieved file content as instruction-like text
mitigations: Add a manual review step before indexing Airbyte outputs into Khoj
Prefix imported content as untrusted in notes
Restrict Khoj retrieval to vetted folders
Use a separate workspace for generated vs. source documents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Khoj indexes personal notes/files and can send queries to a cloud or configured search provider. If the same workspace or exported data flows from Airbyte into Khoj, sensitive business data can be exposed outside the intended boundary. The pair creates a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF Airbyte-managed business data is exported into files indexed by Khoj
IF Khoj is configured to use a cloud search/provider backend
mitigations: Keep Airbyte exports out of Khoj-indexed folders
Disable external search providers in Khoj for sensitive collections
Use separate credentials and storage locations
Review indexed documents for secrets before ingestion
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before indexing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and egress broadly, while Khoj reads filesystem content and maintains a shared index across clients. They do not both write the filesystem, so direct write-write conflict is absent, but they can still contend over shared mutable data sources and indexes if pointed at the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same document repository or export directory
IF Khoj's shared index is updated while Airbyte is refreshing source data
mitigations: Separate source and index directories
Schedule Airbyte syncs and Khoj reindexing at different times
Use read-only mounts for Khoj over Airbyte outputs
Document ownership of each mutable dataset

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data that Khoj may retrieve from indexed documents. Khoj's RAG workflow can then surface that content as authoritative chat output. Because there is no explicit verification layer between them, errors or stale records from Airbyte can cascade into user-facing answers.
conditions: IF Airbyte-generated records are indexed into Khoj
IF users rely on Khoj answers without checking the source documents
mitigations: Mark Airbyte-derived notes with provenance metadata
Require source-link display in Khoj responses
Reindex after Airbyte sync completion
Spot-check a sample of retrieved answers against source data

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or configured search providers. If regulated or residency-sensitive data is moved from Airbyte into Khoj's indexed corpus, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify a direct mismatch, so this is a conditional compliance risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated business data is exported from Airbyte into Khoj
IF Khoj is hosted in a different jurisdiction or retention regime than the source system
mitigations: Classify which datasets may enter Khoj
Exclude regulated collections from indexing
Set retention limits on indexed notes
Document residency and retention for each data flow
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing/redaction
